title: Night Cream Side Effects: What Is Normal and When to Stop
ex: Tingling, redness or new spots after a night cream? Learn what is normal adjustment, what is a real reaction, and how to patch test and start safely.
rt: Night Cream Side Effects: Normal vs Not | Mirc Glow
rd: Night cream side effects explained: normal tingling vs real reactions, the purging myth, kojic acid sensitivity, sunscreen, patch testing and when to stop.
quick: Mild tingling, slight dryness or a few spots in the first week or two can be normal. Burning that lasts, redness the next morning, itching, swelling or a rash mean you should stop. Patch test for three nights, start slowly and wear sunscreen every morning.
facts: Patch test behind the ear for three nights
True purging is linked to retinoids and acids, not plain moisturisers
Kojic acid is typically used at around 1–2% in creams
Some unregulated creams have been found to contain steroids or mercury
